product_family: Document workflow platform covering proposal/quote creation, eSignature, contract management, CPQ (configure-price-quote), Rooms (deal collaboration), payments, and forms/notary; API and CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, etc.) sold as add-ons/tiers on top of the core document platform

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote: "PandaDoc is SOC 2 Type II compliant. We can provide our latest SSAE 18 SOC 2 Type II report."

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27001
certifications.proof_quote: PandaDoc's own Security Practices page attributes this cert to its infrastructure providers, not itself: "Any third-party cloud service provider that PandaDoc utilizes to host and Process Customer Content will have at a minimum, industry standard physical security precautions in place and conform to ISO 27001 or equivalent certification standards." No PandaDoc-domain page claims PandaDoc itself holds an ISO 27001 certificate; only AWS (the host) is described as conforming to it. Third-party aggregator sites claim "PandaDoc is ISO 27001 compliant" but this is not corroborated by any pandadoc.com page and appears to conflate the host's certification with the vendor's.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: "PandaDoc is a HIPAA-compliant eSignature tool that offers the features and safeguards to protect electronic patient health information (PHI)." A Business Associate Agreement (BAA) must be separately requested and signed: "In order to transmit electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI) using PandaDoc and maintain it with HIPAA compliance, customers should sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)."

certifications.name: GDPR (compliance posture)
certifications.proof_quote: "PandaDoc complies with GDPR by processing personal data lawfully, transparently, and only for specific legitimate purposes." Standard DPA available and referenced from the Privacy Notice; PandaDoc acts as Processor with customer as Controller, per the Data Processing Agreement.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: PandaDoc does not claim its own PCI DSS certification; it integrates with certified third-party processors: "PandaDoc integrates with PCI-DSS compliant payment processors to offer payment processing via credit cards." This is the payment processor's certification, not PandaDoc's own.

certifications.name: eIDAS
certifications.proof_quote: PandaDoc's SOC2/HIPAA/GDPR summary page groups eIDAS alongside its other compliance frameworks and links a dedicated eIDAS explainer; eSignatures are positioned as legally binding under eIDAS in the EU. Footer compliance badges on pandadoc.com list eIDAS alongside HIPAA, SOC 2, and GDPR.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on any pandadoc.com page of an ISO/IEC 42001 AI-governance certification.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence found on any pandadoc.com page of CSA STAR registration or certification.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: FedRAMP is referenced only as an AWS infrastructure-level authorization in PandaDoc's compliance page discussion of its cloud host, not as a PandaDoc-held authorization: no public evidence PandaDoc itself is FedRAMP authorized.

certifications.name: CCPA
certifications.proof_quote: PandaDoc provides a "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" mechanism via OneTrust privacy portal linked in the site footer, and its blog/compliance material lists CCPA among supported frameworks alongside SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR.

privacy.ai_training_note: PandaDoc's own AI Addendum (a binding legal document on pandadoc.com) grants PandaDoc a broad license over AI-feature outputs for training: "Customer hereby grants PandaDoc a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, sublicensable, worldwide, fully paid right and license, to use, host, reproduce, display, perform, and modify AI Output to create AI Improvement Data for PandaDoc's AI Training." The Addendum defines 'AI Improvement Data' as derived only from 'anonymized and aggregated AI Output or Usage Data' (i.e. outputs of AI features such as summaries/suggestions, not raw uploaded documents verbatim). Customers may opt out, but only prospectively: "Customers may, at any time, and on a go-forward basis, elect to opt-out of using PandaDoc AI Services." The Addendum does not describe retroactive deletion of already-used AI Improvement Data. This contradicts secondary marketing/press claims circulating that PandaDoc 'does not use customer contract data to train AI models'; the vendor's own legal terms describe a narrower but real anonymized/aggregated training right with a forward-only opt-out.
privacy.data_region: Customer-selectable regional hosting: US or EU (Frankfurt, Germany), per PandaDoc's own Data Residency page: "PandaDoc offers a choice of data center locations. Our Customers may choose between regional versions of our SaaS application, within the US or within the EU." Support/customer-service interactions and some third-party integrations can still move data to the US regardless of the chosen region. Accounts cannot be migrated between the US and EU data centers after creation.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: AES-256: "All data in each location is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and sophisticated encryption keys management."

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: "PandaDoc will encrypt Customer Content in-transit and at rest and will only allow encrypted connections to the Service."

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: "PandaDoc uses external security experts to conduct penetration testing of the Services at least annually and maintains a year-round bug bounty program."

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure / bug bounty
security.value: Public responsible-disclosure program run via HackerOne.

security.name: SSO
security.value: Single sign-on offered for granular document and workspace permissions (per homepage feature summary; plan-tier gating not independently confirmed).

security.name: Cloud hosting / physical security
security.value: Hosted on Amazon AWS; physical data-center security delegated to AWS controls (badging, 24/7 staff, two-factor access).

security.name: Incident notification
security.value: "PandaDoc will notify Customer in writing without undue delay upon PandaDoc becoming aware of confirmed Security Breach."

security.name: Sub-processor transparency
security.value: Published, updated sub-processor list with customer notice requirements.

products.name: Documents / eSignature core
products.data_scope: Document content, signer PII, audit trail/activity metadata
products.notes: Core product across all paid tiers; drag-and-drop editor, signing order, identity verification, notarization add-on.

products.name: CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote)
products.data_scope: Product catalog data, pricing rules, quote/proposal content
products.notes: Upsell module layered on top of core documents; pulls data from connected CRM/product catalog.

products.name: Rooms
products.data_scope: Shared deal documents, buyer/seller collaboration activity
products.notes: Positioned as an enterprise-leaning collaboration surface distinct from single-document signing.

products.name: API / Developer platform
products.data_scope: All document, template, and workspace data exposed programmatically
products.notes: Separate developer terms (Developer Agreement) and security reference documentation apply; used to embed PandaDoc inside customer products.

products.name: Payments
products.data_scope: Payment method tokens routed to PCI-DSS-certified third-party processors, not stored by PandaDoc directly per available evidence
products.notes: PandaDoc integrates with PCI-DSS-compliant processors rather than holding its own PCI certification.

compare.pricing_model: Tiered SaaS subscription (Starter/Business/Enterprise-style tiers implied by site navigation) plus paid add-ons (API, CPQ, Rooms, notary); exact tier names/pricing not captured in this evidence set.
compare.data_residency: Customer-selectable US or EU (Frankfurt) hosting region; no cross-region account migration; support interactions may still touch US systems.

flags: PandaDoc has no dedicated trust-center subdomain (e.g. trust.pandadoc.com); compliance evidence is spread across /security/, /security/compliance/, /legal/security-practices/, and /hipaa/ pages instead of a single hub. This makes self-service verification harder for buyers.

PandaDoc's own Security Practices page attributes ISO 27001 conformance to its third-party cloud hosting providers (AWS), not to PandaDoc itself. Third-party aggregator sites nonetheless describe PandaDoc as 'ISO 27001 compliant.'

PandaDoc's AI Addendum opt-out clause only stops future use ('on a go-forward basis'); it does not describe retroactive deletion of AI Improvement Data already derived from a customer's AI feature usage. Marketing and press summaries claiming PandaDoc 'does not train on customer data' oversimplify the AI Addendum's actual terms, which grant PandaDoc a broad license to use anonymized and aggregated AI output for training absent an opt-out.
PCI DSS is the payment processor's certification, per PandaDoc's own wording, not PandaDoc's own.
SOC 2 report itself is gated behind an NDA request form, not publicly downloadable; the compliance claim is verifiable via PandaDoc's own text, but the underlying report is not independently public.
